Chapter 176: 0173 The First Generation of Weibo Is About to Go Online (For Alliance Leader Book Friend 16011508)

Tao Xue cried for several minutes, finally quieting down to a sob.

The guard thought something had happened. He walked a few steps out of the guardhouse and stopped, then stood there watching the scene with a cigarette dangling from his lips.

He recognized Chen Guiliang.

Only when Tao Xue started wiping her tears did the guard walk over and offer a cigarette. "Boss Chen, back to visit your alma mater?"

"Yeah, just came back to have a look," Chen Guiliang nodded.

The guard said, "The principal isn't here. He probably went to the city to try and get summer classes reinstated."

Chen Guiliang said, "Thanks for the heads-up."

The two of them stood there chatting idly. Tao Xue, both sad and embarrassed, kept her back to the guard, afraid he would remember her face.

After a few more minutes, Tao Xue secretly tugged on the corner of Chen Guiliang's shirt.

Only then did Chen Guiliang say goodbye to the guard and escort Tao Xue back to the girls' dormitory.

On the way, she said she wanted to watch the sunset, so they found a teaching building with an accessible rooftop.

"It's so beautiful," Tao Xue said, standing behind the rooftop railing.

The sun was about to set, grown large and red, and the horizon was filled with magnificently colored, fiery clouds.

The sunlight itself seemed to turn red, making Tao Xue's face appear even more radiant.

Chen Guiliang said, "Yes, it is. So beautiful."

Neither spoke again, silently watching the sunset side by side.

Tao Xue felt this moment was quite nice; at least she wasn't so sad anymore.

As dusk fell, Chen Guiliang walked with Tao Xue around the campus, finally seeing her to the entrance of the girls' dormitory.

Tao Xue walked towards the staircase, then turned back to look and found Chen Guiliang still standing there. So, she put on a smile again, waved, and shouted, "Goodbye, Senior!"

"Goodbye," Chen Guiliang said with a wave.

Tao Xue pretended to be cheerful, hopping up the stairs. Only when she entered the corridor did her energy deflate. She squatted in the hallway, spacing out all by herself.

After composing herself for a long while, Tao Xue stood up and returned to her dorm room.

Fatty had already packed her luggage, apparently planning to go home tomorrow. "You guys were out this whole time?"

"Yeah."

Tao Xue said triumphantly, "Senior even watched the sunset with me, and we walked back through the campus together."

"Sigh, I can only dream," Fatty said, filled with envy.

Tao Xue lay on her bed with a grin, then rolled over to face the wall. The smile vanished, and her eyes grew moist again. She didn't know why she couldn't stop crying; she had rarely ever cried since she was little.

Taking out her phone, Tao Xue sent a text to Chen Guiliang: "Senior, I'm still going to study in the capital next year."

After a long wait, Chen Guiliang finally replied: "Okay. Get some sleep."

Tao Xue picked up a book from beside her pillow; it was the copy of *Dream of the Red Chamber* that Chen Guiliang had sold her. She flipped it open but didn't read the main text, instead specifically looking for the reading notes Chen Guiliang had written inside.

"His handwriting is really ugly," Tao Xue mumbled.

Chen Guiliang stayed at a hotel in the county town that night and went to take his Subject One exam the next day.

At the examination site, there were only six people.

Two of them were the exam proctors.

The four candidates were given a test paper, a pencil, and a scantron sheet.

One person filled in the answers at lightning speed, glancing down at his palm from time to time. With just one look, he could answer several questions.

Despite such obvious cheating, the proctors turned a blind eye.

Chen Guiliang also answered quickly. As a veteran driver, he was very familiar with the basic traffic rules.

After everyone finished and handed in their papers, they all waited right there.

The proctors took the scantron sheets and ran them through the machine on the spot. All four candidates passed.

Since Chen Guiliang had paid extra to expedite the process, their four test results were sent directly to the county's Vehicle Administration Office.

One of the proctors called Chen Guiliang aside and said, "Wait for your instructor's call this afternoon."

"Thank you." Chen Guiliang handed him a pack of cigarettes.

The man became even happier and asked curiously, "Are you the guy from the news who started a company?"

He had remembered the name but wasn't entirely sure.

"Just someone with the same name," Chen Guiliang said.

When Chen Guiliang walked out of the Subject One examination room, Bian Guanyue had already been waiting for a long time.

Back in the capital, Chen Guiliang had promised Bian Guanyue he would come back to visit her maternal grandparents during the summer break.

"How did it go?" Bian Guanyue asked with a smile.

"I passed," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue said, "I'm going to sign up for driving school during the winter break too."

"Don't get your license and then be too scared to drive."

"I'm not that timid."

"You never know."

The two went to buy some gifts, then took a taxi straight to Bian Guanyue's maternal grandparents' home.

Chen Guiliang was calm and composed, but Bian Guanyue was a little nervous.

Bian Guanyue took out her key to open the door. The moment she did, four people in the living room stood up, leaving only a little kid lying on the sofa watching TV.

"These are my grandpa and grandma," Bian Guanyue introduced.

"Hello, Gonggong. Hello, Popo," Chen Guiliang greeted them.

In the local dialect, *Gonggong* and *Popo* actually mean "old sir" and "old lady."

Bian Guanyue added, "This is my uncle and my aunt. Over there is my cousin."

Chen Guiliang quickly greeted them.

"Hello, hello, please sit."

Bian Guanyue's uncle was named Guan Zhiwei. He was a civil servant in the city, having worked his way up to a deputy section chief position through seniority. Her aunt was a doctor at the city hospital, but she didn't treat patients, only dispensed medicine in the pharmacy.

The couple usually lived in the city and had made a special trip back to the county this time.

As for the cousin, he was still in junior high this year. He didn't greet the guest, only caring about lying on the sofa and watching TV.

"Come over and greet him!" Guan Zhiwei scolded his son.

The cousin stood up lazily. "Hello, big brother."

"Hello," Chen Guiliang nodded.

The grandparents and the aunt all went to the kitchen to get busy, bringing out dishes, bowls, and chopsticks, while also keeping an eye on the fish that was still cooking in the pot.

The uncle was in charge of chatting with Chen Guiliang.

Bian Guanyue brought the cat, Sanmao, over. "Look, he's gotten so big. He was just a tiny thing when we bought him."

Chen Guiliang played with the cat while making small talk with her uncle.

Since the two men had just met, it wasn't appropriate to ask too many personal questions. Their conversation soon drifted to domestic and international politics.

"Xiao Chen, do you know about the series of terrorist attacks in London?"

"I heard about it, but I'm not too clear on the details."

"The day before, London had just won the bid for the 2012 Olympics, and the very next day they were hit by a terrorist attack. A full 52 people died! It must have been premeditated, specifically to sabotage the Olympics."

"That's possible. Uncle, you have sharp insight."

"It's easy to figure these things out. When our country hosts the Olympics, we'll have to be on guard as well."

"Of course. There will definitely be people trying to cause trouble. There are already many lawless elements online..."

After talking about foreign affairs for a while, they started on domestic ones.

The aunt finished setting the table and called out with a smile, "Come and eat!"

Everyone went to wash their hands and sat down around the table.

Guan Zhiwei took out a bottle of Wuliangye. "I'll have a couple of drinks with Xiao Chen."

"No, thank you. I have to take my Subject Two exam this afternoon," Chen Guiliang said.

"Then you really can't drink." Guan Zhiwei put the liquor back in the corner.

The grandmother busied herself serving soup to Chen Guiliang and using clean chopsticks to put food on his plate, so enthusiastic that even Bian Guanyue felt a little embarrassed.

The grandfather praised Chen Guiliang for writing good poetry.

As they were talking, the driving instructor called to inform him of the specific time and location for his test. He also asked if he wanted to practice a few times beforehand.

Chen Guiliang hung up the phone and continued to shoot the breeze with Bian Guanyue's uncle.

"The Greater Mekong Subregion Economic Cooperation summit was held in Caiyun Province. Do you know about that?"

"Yes, the southwest region, especially Caiyun Province, is about to see accelerated development."

"See? Xiao Chen is a businessman, alright. He immediately understands the national development strategy! The country is playing a big game of chess; the effects will only be visible in ten years."

"Uncle, you have a good grasp of domestic and foreign affairs too. Most people don't pay attention to this."

"Haha, I just casually read the news."

Chen Guiliang, who was often a motormouth in public, spent most of the meal playing the straight man, throwing in a bit of flattery from time to time.

He had thoroughly charmed Guan Zhiwei!

After the meal, Chen Guiliang sat for a little while longer before taking his leave to go take his Subject Two exam.

Bian Guanyue walked him downstairs.

The grandmother even stuffed a bag of rather expensive tea into Chen Guiliang's hands, telling him to take it back for his father.

After the two youngsters left, a family meeting immediately commenced in the living room.

The grandmother said, "This young man is quite nice, very polite."

The uncle commented, "Not just polite, but also very knowledgeable. No wonder his business is doing so well; he has a very profound understanding of domestic and international situations."

The aunt retorted, "So being able to chat with you makes him knowledgeable? If he were in the same work unit as you, he could sell you out and you'd still be counting the money for him."

The uncle laughed, "I'm not a fool."

The aunt said, "Some of the things you two talked about, I didn't understand. But I could tell that Xiao Chen was just humoring you, like indulging a child. He was saying whatever you wanted to hear."

The uncle looked puzzled.

The grandfather said, "He's not simple, that one. His mind works very well. If Guanguan is with him, she'll probably be talked into circles."

The grandmother said, "I think he's great. He's talented, handsome, and has a bright future."

At the Subject Two examination site, there was only Chen Guiliang.

It was clearly a last-minute arrangement.

There was no electronic monitoring equipment, just an examiner with a small notebook.

For things like the two front corners of the parallel parking space, there were even two bamboo poles stuck in the ground to help the learner see if they could back in.

As long as you slipped the examiner a good pack of cigarettes beforehand, even if a wheel fell off the single-plank bridge, the examiner could pretend he saw nothing.

Chen Guiliang hadn't driven a manual in a long time, so he practiced a bit with the instructor's car before the test.

After re-familiarizing himself, he naturally passed on the first try.

The instructor felt it was a very easy job. He'd earned this money so easily, it was like picking it up off the ground.

And then, he recognized Chen Guiliang...

Daxia Chen was a local celebrity!

The next day, he passed Subject Three on the first try as well and got his driver's license that same afternoon.

Chen Guiliang was looking over his new license when his secretary called:

"President Chen, the agreement between Kaixinwang and China Mobile is almost finalized. It's a fifty-fifty split, just like with Tencent's Mobile QQ. China Mobile will launch a special 'mini-blog' package for Kaixinwang."

"For users who send and receive mini-blogs, the monthly package fee is 15 yuan, which includes sending and receiving 2,000 messages for free. If you exceed the package limit, each message sent will cost 0.1 yuan. Forwards count as well."

Damn, China Mobile was a real shark.

The person sending the microblog had to pay, and the person receiving it also had to pay.

Fortunately, users could choose not to subscribe to the wireless value-added service, in which case the microblogs they posted could only be seen on a computer. Even if they did subscribe, when sending a specific microblog, they could choose whether or not to send it to users' mobile phones.

This was the prototype of Weibo. Limited by mobile phones and communication technology, it had to transition slowly like this.

People without mobile phones could use it on their computers.

People with mobile phones could also choose to only use it on their computers.

Only people with both a mobile phone and spare cash would subscribe to the monthly Weibo plan to receive microblog text messages on their phones.

In the United States, a similar service wouldn't appear until next year. This time, Chen Guiliang was leading a global trend.

The top priority was to strengthen information moderation!

In the other timeline, the first to scale up Weibo in China was actually "Fanfou," founded by Meituan's CEO Wang. Its user count had already surpassed one million at the time.

Because microblogs could be sent directly to users' phones, certain individuals and forces at the time used "Fanfou" to spread extremely sensitive information, directly leading to "Fanfou" being forcibly shut down for over a year.

In the second month of "Fanfou's" shutdown, Sina seized the opportunity to launch its own Weibo.

By the time "Fanfou" came back online, Sina Weibo had already become dominant!

(End of this chapter)
